assessments.reasoning: GPL [29011,29514) is the counterpart in the 29 June 2007 GPLv3 edition. It names AGPL version 3, requires one combined work, retains GPL terms on the GPL-covered part and identifies the combination as the object of the special network rules. That last provision defeats an interpretation confining their effect to an isolated AGPL component.

AGPL [28300,28957) supplies the referenced requirements, including their triggers, offer terms and GPLv3 source-inclusion sentence. A combination lacking supported remote interaction does not acquire an unconditional public source-offer duty from the GPL cross-reference.

limitations: This finding concerns the two named version-3 editions and the specified combined work. The licenses alone cannot establish a deployment's combined-work status or whether its network-offer conditions are met.
reasoning: GPLv3 §13 permits linking or combining its covered work with an AGPLv3-licensed work into a single work and conveying the result. GPLv3 remains on the GPL-covered part. The clause applies AGPLv3 §13's special network-interaction requirements to the combination as such. The AGPL-side permission retains AGPLv3 on its covered part.
